course.title: Visual Studio Code Masterclass for DevOps and AI
course.subtitle: Set up VS Code as a DevOps engineer's workbench, learn its words and interface, and give AI coding agents the instructions and limits they need.
course.description:
Kubernetes YAML, Terraform, Dockerfiles, Bash, Git and remote servers: most DevOps engineers touch all of them in one editor. This free course makes that editor work for you, and shows how to work with AI coding agents safely.

## What you'll learn
- **Why VS Code fits DevOps work,** and how it understands YAML, Terraform and Dockerfiles through extensions and language servers.
- **Its vocabulary:** workspaces, the Command Palette, extensions, profiles, snippets, tasks and Dev Containers.
- **The whole interface,** area by area, on a real DevOps repository, and how to get a lost layout back.
- **AI coding agents with guardrails:** CLAUDE.md instruction files, the .claude folders, permissions and deny rules that really block an agent.

## Why this course
- **Free, practical and on a real repository** you download and open yourself.
- **Hands-on labs** for the setup and AI lessons, running Claude Code in Docker.
- **Quizzes** after each lesson.

## Who it's for
DevOps, cloud and software engineers who want a productive, shareable editor setup and safe habits with AI coding assistants.
objectives: Explain why VS Code suits DevOps work and how extensions and language servers understand your files
Use workspaces, the Command Palette, profiles, snippets, tasks and Dev Containers
Find your way around every area of the VS Code interface and recover a lost layout
Write CLAUDE.md files that give an AI coding agent your build commands, conventions and pitfalls
Configure the .claude folders with permissions and deny rules, and verify what really applies
requirements: A computer that can run VS Code (Windows, macOS or Linux)
Docker for the AI agent labs
No prior VS Code experience needed

lessons.title: Why VS Code is the DevOps engineer's editor
lessons.summary: YAML, Terraform, Dockerfiles, Bash, Git and remote servers in one window: what VS Code is, how it understands your files, and a first look on a real DevOps repository.

lessons.title: VS Code vocabulary: workspaces, extensions and Dev Containers
lessons.summary: Workspace, Command Palette, extension, language server, profile, snippet, task and Dev Container, one at a time: an everyday example, an animation, then the real screen.

lessons.title: A complete tour of the VS Code interface
lessons.summary: Every area of the window, what it's called, why it's there and when a DevOps engineer uses it, on a real DevOps repository, plus the shortcuts that get you back when a layout is lost.

lessons.title: CLAUDE.md in depth: instructions for AI coding agents
lessons.summary: Where CLAUDE.md files live, the order they load, imports and rules, what /init writes, and what to keep in or out, so Claude Code knows your build, conventions and pitfalls.

lessons.title: Write CLAUDE.md for a real repository
lessons.summary: On a sample repository with Claude Code running in Docker: /init writes a first CLAUDE.md, you trim it, add rules and an import, then check exactly what Claude loads.

lessons.title: The .claude folders: settings, permissions and deny rules
lessons.summary: The global and project .claude folders of Claude Code: what goes where, which wins, what goes into git, and proof that a deny rule really blocks Claude.
